title: King by another’s strength
literal_meaning: By Kichaka’s strength of arm, Virata is king.
meaning_odia: ନିଜ ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ଅପେକ୍ଷା ଅନ୍ୟର ବଳ ବା ସାହସରେ କାହାର ଅଧିକାର ଓ ପ୍ରତିପତ୍ତି ରହିବା। କୀଚକର ବଳରେ ବିରାଟଙ୍କ ରାଜତ୍ୱର ଛବି ଦେଇ ଅନ୍ୟର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭରତାକୁ ଦେଖାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The title belongs to one person, while the strength sustaining it comes from another. The inspected proverb gloss applies the saying critically to someone whose position or advantages depend on another person’s courage or power.
usage_example: A nominal leader claims all the credit, though a capable colleague handles every difficult negotiation. Someone recalls this saying about the strength behind the title. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: The saying draws on Kichaka and King Virata from the Mahabharata. The inspected source gloss casts Kichaka as the source of the force supporting Virata’s rule, turning the two names into a compact image of dependent authority.

witnesses.locator: Page11, single line beginning କୀଚକ ବାହୁବଳେ.
witnesses.note: Rendered page inspected17November2026; uploaded spelling ରଜା retained.
Full saying with ରାଜା rather than uploaded ରଜା. Gloss explicitly describes authority or advantages gained through another’s strength or courage; supplies epic frame.

odia_summary: ଅଧିକାର ଜଣକର, ତାହାକୁ ଧରିରଖିବାର ବଳ ଆଉ ଜଣକର।
english_summary: One person holds the title; another supplies the strength behind it.
